summary: Pigeon River Middle lookout in Pigeon River Country State Forest; no longer standing, anchor-leg stubs remain, and a 2020 trail reaches the site.

facts.status_note: No longer standing; the ends of its three galvanized steel anchor legs still stick up 6 inches above the ground.

access.note: The Towerman's Watch Pathway is open to hikers in summer and snowshoers in winter; mountain bikers and equestrians are not allowed.

visit.trail_note: 3.7-mile loop from the Pigeon River Country headquarters; the former tower site is about 2 miles in.

events.note: A cabin for towermen was constructed at the Pigeon River tower site, reported in the 1937-38 Ninth Biennial Report.
Towerman's Watch Pathway was built, partly because of the former tower site's location and history.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The forest lookouts site calls it the Pigeon River lookout; the trail guide calls it the Pigeon River Middle Fire Tower. Treated as one tower because both sit on the same Pigeon River site; no source says so outright.

sources.title: Pigeon River Country SF: Towerman's Watch Pathway

notes_for_editor: Identity of the forest-lookouts Pigeon River entry with the trail guide's Middle tower is inferred from the shared site, not stated by a source. The build date is not in any source found. The michigan.gov trail page returned 403, and the Press and Guide 2019 article did not contain tower text in the cached copy. Brief elevation (337 m) is not supported by any source found. Brief coordinates match the OSM node.
